System blueprint

A focused SaaS launch

Turn a specific customer problem into a useful first product release. Connect discovery, interface design, implementation, onboarding, and measurement around the core workflow rather than an unbounded feature list.

Level 2Choose a capability

A broad idea can expand into a product that is difficult to build, test, and explain. A launch needs an agreed user, a valuable first workflow, a clear scope, and a team that owns the product after release.

Useful outputs

  • A product specification, reviewed prototype, and prioritized first-release scope.
  • A tested application with selected authentication, data, billing, and notification workflows.
  • A deployment and support handover with administrator guidance.
  • An activation and retention measurement plan and next-phase backlog.

Inputs we need

  • A defined user problem, core workflow, business owner, and first-release priorities.
  • Approved data, permissions, branding, payment requirements, and provider access.
  • Acceptance criteria, deployment expectations, support ownership, and product value-event definitions.
Level 3Explore a focus

Define and design

Identify the first user and value event, prioritize the essential workflow, and review the prototype and acceptance criteria. Define what belongs in the first release and what should wait.

Build and connect

Implement the application and agreed data, access, billing, and notification paths. Validate provider accounts and test modes; engineers review code and important permission boundaries.

Human expertise

Own the judgment.

Product owners approve scope, positioning, user experience, and commercial decisions. Engineers own architecture, code review, access checks, testing, release quality, and operational handover.

AI assistance

Support the process.

AI can assist research, prototyping, implementation preparation, and documentation. Generated work is reviewed and tested; product commitments and final acceptance remain with the responsible people.
